fixture_sha256_matched.rule: candidates in order: sha256 of the fixture file on disk at score time; then, for a runtime fixture only, derived_from.sha256. First match wins and is recorded. No candidate matches -> tampered true, exit 2. The scorecard also records tamper_scope: 'certified' on a fixture_file match, 'authored-only: ... the runtime file on disk (sha256 ...) is not certified by a match on that digest' on an authored_derived_from match, so the weaker match can never be read as runtime-file integrity.

blocker: LR-01 cannot score green under either schema, and this card did not make it: its acceptance block is prose only. Frozen runtime/LR-01.json (and authored fixtures/LR-01.json) score exit 1 with exactly eight required checks unverifiable -- check.1-4 (prose: 'python3 -c ... exits 0', 'pytest -q ... exits 0', 'resolve(...) raises ... AND leaves exactly one ledger row', 'grep -c ... prints 9'), con.1-3 ('never delete or weaken the isinstance(scope, Scope) guard', 'never delete or edit a test', 'never edit the fixture or its pinned sources' -- no deterministic predicate), repair.main (correct_action is 130-char prose, no accept_literal). This is identical for both schemas (PARITY), so it is a fixture-surface gap, not an adapter gap. Fixing it means a card that owns the fixtures: express the acceptance checks as structured dicts / log-carried artifact checks and add repair.accept_literal, then re-run tests_score_adapter.py's GREEN_RUNTIME pattern against the real LR-01. Consequence: the third pillar stays unmeasurable on the real suite until that card lands.

The card's WRITE PATHS exclude QUALITY-RUBRIC.md, so it was left untouched. One optional precision, if a later card wants it: QUALITY-RUBRIC.md 'The three ways a high score could be faked' item 1 ('Defence: the fixture is hashed at score time and compared with the `fixture_sha256` the harness wrote at run start.') could add: 'For a runtime fixture the run may instead record the authored fixture's digest (derived_from); the scorecard names which digest matched (`fixture_sha256_matched`) and states that such a match does not certify the runtime file (`tamper_scope`).'
